mared.scripts.help.1: Project → New project creates an empty workspace. Select a project in the left tree; its files, tabs and drafts stay together.
mared.scripts.help.2: File → New file / New folder. Right-click a folder for the same actions. A simple name uses the selected folder; a path containing / starts at the project root.
mared.scripts.help.3: Ctrl+S saves the active source. Each open document retains its own Undo/Redo and editor position.
mared.scripts.help.4: The tab close button checkpoints a recovery draft. Reopening restores unsaved text.
mared.scripts.help.5: Files: config/mared/script_projects/<project>. External IDEs can edit them; use Project → Refresh afterwards.
mared.scripts.help.6: External changes are never deliberately overwritten. Recovery is in .genesis-recovery; resolve conflicts outside the game.
mared.scripts.help.7: Run → Run Java / Ctrl+R compiles a snapshot including open drafts. The same menu provides stop, main class (e.g. demo.Main), and output copying.
mared.scripts.help.8: Java runs locally with your OS permissions in a separate process; this is not a security sandbox. No game API or server execution yet.
mared.scripts.help.9: Defaults: 20 s compilation, 10 s execution, heap 128 MiB, output 64 KiB per process. Client Java must include jdk.compiler (full JDK 21). Drafts are recorded after 0.5 s without typing and on GUI close; a crash before recording may lose latest changes.
mared.scripts.bad_entry: Use a class name such as Main or demo.Main, without arguments or paths.

mared.scripts.result.INPUT_ERROR: Java: invalid sources or external file conflict
mared.scripts.source_limit: Java: open sources exceed the 16 MiB limit.
mared.scripts.help.10: Run → Libraries folder copies the libraries path. Add JARs and their dependencies there; the next Java run uses them without restarting.
mared.scripts.help.11: Up to 32 JARs, 8 MiB each, 64 MiB total. No folders or links inside libraries. Maven/Gradle, native DLLs, automatic installation and annotation processors are not connected. JAR Manifest Class-Path is rejected; resources inside ordinary JARs are available via ClassLoader.
mared.scripts.help.13: Project → Export project creates a ZIP of the supported full tree with open drafts, binary assets and empty folders. Build caches and recovery are excluded. Sources are not saved. Review contents before sharing.
mared.scripts.help.12: Run → Resources folder copies resources. Java Run exposes these through ClassLoader, not as an automatic Minecraft resource pack. Limits: 512 files, 8 MiB each, 32 MiB total.
mared.scripts.help.14: Project → Add Gradle build creates a Java/application build for src/resources/libraries/tests. Existing build files stay intact. Direct Java Run supports root sources; configure Gradle source roots in the build file.

mared.scripts.help.15: Ctrl+Shift+P: configure JDK home and Gradle Wrapper JAR, then check build tools. Configuration is available before creating a project. A full JDK 21+ is required; properties must be next to the Wrapper JAR. Machine paths stay local and are not exported.

mared.scripts.help.16: File → Save all saves open edits in the selected project. Run → Build Gradle / Ctrl+B uses saved files; drafts block builds. Configure the Gradle task through Run.
mared.scripts.help.17: Gradle runs with your OS permissions and may download dependencies. Bottom logs show progress; stop through Run. Timeout: 10 minutes. build/libs and build/distributions artifacts appear in logs.
mared.scripts.help.18: The tree shows text files, binary assets and empty folders. Left-click expands a folder; right-click opens actions. Ctrl+Shift+E reveals the open file. Top tabs switch documents; the wheel scrolls tabs.

mared.scripts.workflow: How to work with a project
mared.scripts.build_no_artifacts: No archives found in standard build/libs or build/distributions in the project or its modules. Check the report and task configuration.
mared.scripts.build_report_note: Last completed build for this project in this session. Saving code does not update the JAR: build again. This list does not identify which JAR is the installable mod. Building does not install a mod or apply it to the current game.
mared.scripts.workflow.tools_note: JDK 21+ and Wrapper files were checked. This does not run Gradle or verify dependency downloads or project compatibility with this JDK.
mared.scripts.workflow.0: 1. Project → Import folder, New project or New NeoForge project. Import creates a working copy; the original folder is unchanged.
mared.scripts.workflow.1: 2. Choose a file in Explorer. File → New file / New folder. The destination folder appears at the bottom of Explorer. Right-click an entry for file operations.
mared.scripts.workflow.2: 3. Edit text. File → Save or Save all. A recovery draft does not replace saving before a build. Changes are written to the Genesis working copy.
mared.scripts.workflow.3: 4. Building requires a configured Gradle project, not just .java files. Import one or create a NeoForge starter. Run → JDK: choose the full JDK 21+ root, not bin or java.exe.
mared.scripts.workflow.4: 5. Run → Check build tools. The project uses its own Wrapper when present. Otherwise configure a Gradle Wrapper JAR with gradle-wrapper.properties next to it.
mared.scripts.workflow.5: 6. Save all → Run → Refresh Gradle tasks → Choose Gradle task. Filter by name, module or description. Selection only saves the task; then use Build Gradle. Manual task input remains available. See Task discovery report for listing errors.
mared.scripts.workflow.6: 7. Run → Last build result: report and root/subproject archive paths. Get build archive creates a separate verified copy and copies its path. For custom directories, consult the log and Gradle configuration.
mared.scripts.workflow.7: 8. Project → Project path: working folder. Export creates a ZIP archive and may include open drafts without saving them to the working copy. Import is not a live link to the original folder.
mared.scripts.workflow.8: 9. A standalone JAR depends on its code and dependencies. The NeoForge starter does not require MaRed. Installing a new mod JAR still requires restarting the game; Run Java uses a separate process, not the current world.

mared.scripts.diagnostic_notes: Recognizes standard javac error/warning messages (including Russian output) and Gradle Build file/Settings file/Script positions. Navigation targets the project that built. Open drafts are retained. Positions belong to the last completed build and may shift after edits. Lines and columns are clamped to the current text; without a column, the cursor goes to the beginning of the line. External files, unknown formats and messages without positions are shown as text. Zero recognized messages does not mean build success: check the status and full report. Live diagnostics, underlines, quick fixes and a language server are not included yet.
mared.scripts.artifact_help: How to get a built JAR
mared.scripts.artifact_notes:
Choose a discovered archive: Genesis creates a separate copy in .artifacts beside the projects and copies its full path. SHA-256 and size are checked before delivery, during copying and afterwards. Changed or missing files are refused: build again. This does not install into mods or hot-reload code.

Discovery checks build/libs and build/distributions in the root and nested modules. Custom output directories are not recognized. The list describes files found after a successful task; it does not prove that task rebuilt them. For example, test may leave an earlier JAR.

Sources/javadoc labels are inferred from filenames. An ordinary JAR label does not prove it is a mod or contains every dependency. Only the selected file is delivered, without dependencies. Discovery may be incomplete when limits are reached; check the build report. JAR structure and source identity are checked. Mod / bundled-mod labels distinguish releases. External runtime libraries still require explicit installation or embedding.

mared.scripts.dependencies_note: Requires build.gradle. Mod dependencies and Jar-in-Jar require NeoGradle. Maven dependencies use Gradle, not direct Java execution. Install the output of jarJar when embedding libraries. Optional mods are compile-only; your code must handle their absence. Library and local JARs are not automatically bundled into a release. Use Embed for a NeoForge library that must travel inside the mod. Optional integrations can be tested with genesis.optionalMods=true in gradle.properties.
